page: UpCloud PREMIUM-1xCPU-2GB is an entry-level virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single shared vCPU based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2.0 GB of system memory, a 25 GB local SSD for storage, and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 vector extensions, cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI, and bit manipulation instructions.

Benchmark data reveals highly polarized performance characteristics. Due to the modern AMD EPYC architecture, single-core processing is highly efficient, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. However, because the server is limited to a single shared vCPU, multi-core and overall system benchmarks are constrained. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and static web serving throughput fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is also a bottleneck, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the bottom 10% and read-only memory bandwidth categorized as weak.

This server offers a highly cost-efficient entry point for workloads that do not require sustained multi-threaded performance or high memory throughput. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation and low memory capacity, which limits its utility for resource-intensive applications. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded tasks, basic utility scripting, low-traffic web serving, or small-scale development and testing environments where single-core burst performance is beneficial but overall resource demands remain minimal.
